department: Agribusiness, Food Industry Mgmt, and Ag Science
description: Combine your passion for crops or livestock with business skills to manage anything from a family farm to a global company. The only program of its kind in California, it offers a strong foundation in agribusiness—covering marketing, accounting, food laws, and more—while preparing you to navigate industry challenges and tailor your path to your career goals.

department: Agribusiness, Food Industry Mgmt, and Ag Science
description: A degree in agricultural science will equip you with the knowledge and skills needed to address critical challenges in sustainable food production, environmental stewardship and global food security. Blending science, technology and hands-on experience, this interdisciplinary program prepares you to work in general agriculture, animal science, agribusiness, agricultural education and research.

Turn your passion for animals into a career by working alongside veterinarians, assisting with surgeries, and taking x-rays of animals big and small. As the only 4-year AVMA-accredited Veterinary Technician program on the West Coast, you'll graduate ready to take the VTNE and become a licensed registered veterinary technologist (RVTg).

Get ready for a career in the thriving animal industry with hands-on learning and access to more animals than any other Southern California college. The Animal Science general option prepares you for animal-focused careers beyond veterinary medicine, offering broad coursework across species and specialties to build a strong foundation in animal sciences.

Be on your way to achieving your dream of becoming a veterinarian or going to graduate school with our in-depth and hands-on curriculum. The Pre-Vet/Graduate School option meets the admission requirements of most veterinary medicine programs, and it equips you for advanced study in fields related to animal care or husbandry, including animal nutrition, meat science and more.

Design a clothing line from scratch and bring it to life alongside fellow artists and visionaries. Get your hands on hardware, your eyes on industry-level software and see your designs worn across campus. Just outside L.A., you'll tap into global fashion trends, build a standout portfolio, and launch your career in the fashion industry.

Help shape culture by bringing fashion to the masses. Study fashion retailing in a $400 billion U.S. industry. Build a foundation in market research, product development, distribution and brand marketing, then focus on retail, wholesale or brand development to tailor your degree.

Revolutionize how we produce and consume fashion with a focus on sustainability. Build a strong foundation in apparel design and production, then explore ways to reduce the environmental impact of this global industry. Learn to innovate in textiles, dyeing, printing and supply chain management.

Grow your career and feed the future. We emphasize high-impact teaching to develop a skilled, inclusive workforce in sustainable fruit, vegetable, agronomic, and tree crops; urban and controlled environment agriculture; and plant science fields like irrigation, arboriculture, sports turf, botanical gardens, and natural resource conservation.

Apply creativity and science in the Culinology® option, blending food science and culinary arts to create innovative foods for retail and food service. Take courses in Food Science and Culinary Arts in one of the few RCA-approved programs in the U.S.

Create the next food trend or prepare for science-based careers. The General Option offers a flexible path to graduation with core food science requirements and electives that support pre-professional tracks or minors like nutrition, business, and plant-based foods.

Explore food through biochemistry, processing, safety, and packaging. This IFT-approved option blends science and theory, preparing you for careers as a food chemist, microbiologist, or technologist—or for graduate study in science or tech fields.

Passionate about food? Curious about how it works with our bodies to fuel our future? The Dietetics option mixes science with practical experience, preparing you for advanced studies to become a registered dietitian or dietetic technician and make a real impact in food, health and wellness.

Fuel your passion for health and wellness with the Nutrition and Health option, where nutrition science connects with skills to support healthier lives. Explore disease prevention, well-being, and the psychology of health. Blend science, creativity, and hands-on experience to prepare for a rewarding career in nutrition.

Explore complex nutrition issues through core courses, labs, and health sciences. Choose from two tracks: Pre-professional for careers in medicine, dentistry, veterinary or graduate studies, and Animal Nutrition for a focus on animal health. This program emphasizes nutrition's role in health and disease to prepare you for careers in research, healthcare, and specialized fields.

Build a strong foundation in accounting, business law, economics and marketing. Courses like cost, intermediate and tax accounting, auditing and accounting information systems blend theory, tech and practice. Students are prepared for careers in public, private and government accounting.

Build business apps, strengthen cybersecurity, or harness business intelligence—students gain hands-on experience that prepares them to lead. Our learn-by-doing approach drives innovation in information systems. Employers praise our grads for their skills, mindset and leadership. Join CIS and help shape the future of tech and business.

Combine management and technology skills to stay ahead in fast-changing business environments. Gain hands-on experience with tools like RFID, SAP, Dreamweaver and Android APIs. Explore how e-business and supply chain management create competitive advantage—and take the first step toward shaping the future of business.

Build expertise in finance, real estate or business law through a curriculum that blends theory and hands-on learning. Prepare for careers in financial analysis, CFA® certification, real estate brokerage or contract management. Gain practical skills, leadership insight and credentials to thrive in today’s competitive business landscape.

Prepare for a global career by building business expertise and deepening your understanding of culture, language, economics and politics. Gain skills in international business management and tailor your studies to a region or functional area of interest. Learn to lead, adapt and succeed in today’s fast-changing global economy.

Develop skills in management, HR and entrepreneurship through hands-on training in leadership, hiring, ethics, diversity, training, employment law and startups. Choose an emphasis in Management and Leadership, Human Resources Management or Entrepreneurship to shape a career focused on people, strategy and organizational success.

Understand how to identify market needs and develop strategies to meet them through product, pricing, promotion and distribution decisions. Study internal and external factors that influence marketing plans, and gain the tools to analyze, plan and execute campaigns that drive value and performance in a competitive business landscape.

Design, improve and manage the processes that drive business success. Learn to use technology and data to plan, make decisions and streamline operations. Gain a broad foundation, then specialize in Supply Chain Management, Management of Technology or Service Operations to shape efficient, tech-forward organizations.

Explore aerodynamics, astrodynamics, propulsion, flight mechanics, systems engineering, and aerospace vehicle design—literal rocket science and more! Gain hands-on experience through industry-simulated projects, research, and internships. With focuses in aeronautics and astronautics, you'll graduate ready to launch your dream aerospace career.

Make a transformational impact by creating products people rely on every day. Prepare to produce life-saving medications, develop trendsetting cosmetics, implement sustainable energy, or ensure food safety. Study chemistry, biology, physics, reaction engineering, materials science, and biotechnology to enter diverse industries.

Deal with developing products and processes based on understanding the structure of materials. The goal of the materials engineer is to understand the structure of materials (at the micro- or the nano level) to improve their properties and ultimately their performance. Materials engineers apply this knowledge to the production, selection, and utilization of materials. Since engineers are called upon to work with new ideas and materials, the engineering graduate with a minor in Materials Engineering is very well prepared to respond to such a challenge and thus has a career advantage.

Contribute to the health and protection of populations and the environment in one of the fastest-growing fields in engineering. Prepare for lifesaving work in developing systems for water quality, pollution reduction, energy and sustainability. Study air and water quality, biology, geology, water supply systems and more, and lay the foundation for your dream career.

Design the infrastructure of modern society—buildings, traffic systems, and water resources. Gain a strong foundation in structural analysis, materials science, and fluid mechanics. With small classes, technical electives, and one of the largest civil engineering programs in the U.S., you'll be ready to build your dream career.

Play an instrumental role in the critical field of land management and development. Build upon your education in civil engineering with courses in surveying, remote sensing, photogrammetry, geographical information systems and global positioning systems. Lay the groundwork for your dream career as a licensed civil engineer, land surveyor or land development engineer.

Lead in the construction industry by blending civil engineering and business. Learn structural engineering, project management, and cost estimation. Hands-on labs and practical coursework prepare you for careers in commercial, heavy-civil, or residential construction.

Channel your passion for technology into solutions for an increasingly computerized world. Apply theories and principles of physics and mathematics to the study of circuits, electronics, software, hardware and digital system design to solve technical problems. With over 15 electrical and computer engineering laboratories, you will gain the hands-on experience needed to achieve your dream career.

Design the electrical systems that power our world. Get hands-on with circuits, software, hardware, and more in labs and projects. Develop technical and communication skills with expert faculty and prepare for a successful career in electrical engineering.

Become an instrumental member of the engineering field by bridging mechanical and thermofluid systems with electronics and control systems. With an emphasis on applied design, operation, and troubleshooting of electromechanical systems, you will study materials strength, heat transfer, programming, robotics and more on the way to your dream career.

Explore electronics, computers, and communications to help power the future. Study digital and communication electronics, controls, robotics, and more. Develop teamwork, technical, and communication skills for success in the industry.

Transform complex systems to make organizations more productive, sustainable and successful. Join systems engineering, operations research, supply chains and logistics, and more to improve processes that include people, technology and resources. In industrial engineering, you will combine the human and technical elements of manufacturing and production.

Delve into the study of physics, materials science, thermodynamics and mechanical design to plan, optimize and manage the systems that produce the products we use every day. You will build a solid foundation in production processes, properties of materials, computers and automation, teamwork, and professional communication, then put your skills to the test in our state-of-the-art lab facilities.

Become an innovator behind modern essentials like engines and HVAC systems. Build a strong foundation in mechanics, energy systems, and design. With hands-on labs, small classes, and industry-informed faculty, shape your path toward a rewarding mechanical engineering career.

Design and shape the world around you, while also learning about the people, places, programs, and purposes of buildings and human environments. You will become an innovative problem solver and build skills in a broad spectrum of visual communication tools and methods, design technologies, and design information management.

Explore the artistic legacies of historical periods, regions and cultural traditions worldwide. In Art History, you will immerse yourself in the study of production, reception and experience of art, architecture, design, mass media and other artifacts. Our program provides the flexibility to choose electives in a series of disciplines to shape your degree to your career goals.

Create images that inform, persuade, and inspire while considering cultural, societal, and technological impacts. Gain skills to design across mediums and build a portfolio that showcases your creativity and technical expertise. With hands-on projects and industry connections, you’ll be ready to make a meaningful impact in design.

Positively impact lives and the environment through Landscape Architecture. Restore wetlands, design habitats, grow food, and remove toxins from rainwater. At the intersection of science, art, and ecology, this field blends design, engineering, and sustainability to shape healthier, more beautiful communities.

Make a transformational impact in housing, public space, and placemaking, contributing to equitable urban and regional (re)development. Through classroom and community-based learning, you’ll gain practical knowledge of history, theory, and methods to navigate complex professional and political settings ethically and effectively.

Build the physical and organizational backbone that keeps cities running. Explore infrastructure shaping the built environment—transportation, power, water, and more. Learn about policy, planning methods, land use, regulation, transportation modes, innovation, and equity in infrastructure systems.

Become a steward of sustainable communities and help regions adapt to environmental change. This option blends science, ethics, and policy to address diverse environmental issues. Explore planning processes that navigate uncertainty in natural and social systems, from local ecosystems to global climate change.

Improve the well-being of communities by creating inviting, functional public spaces. The urban design option is designed to explore ideas around placemaking, tools, and techniques that make cities beautiful, livable, and meaningful to their inhabitants.

The Biology program provides students with a broad view of biological processes, a strong theoretical foundation paired with extensive hands-on experiences in diverse labs. Choose from emphases in Botany, Cell and Molecular Biology, Microbiology, Neuroscience and Physiology, or Zoology.

Blend biology and chemistry to prepare students for real-world applications. Gain theoretical and practical knowledge in cell and molecular biology, then focus your studies in areas such as physiology, biochemistry, food and agriculture, the environment, or biotechnology policy and business.

Tackle environmental issues through hands-on study of conservation and biodiversity. With emphases in Ecology or Environmental Microbiology, the Environmental Biology program includes fieldwork and internships to prepare you for impactful careers.

Understand the universe through the intersection of chemistry and physics. Study general, organic, physical, inorganic, and analytical chemistry. Work alongside expert faculty in advanced labs. With an American Chemical Society emphasis, you'll be ready for careers in research, industry, or graduate studies.

See the world at a molecular level. Explore chemical processes in living organisms with courses in molecular biology, enzymology, and metabolic pathways. Gain hands-on experience with lab techniques. You'll be prepared for impactful careers in pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, and medical research.

Discover the world at its most basic level through theoretical, practical, and experimental training. Explore atoms, biomolecules, chemical reactions, and matter’s composition. Work in cutting-edge labs alongside faculty. Choose from ACS, Biochemistry, or General options to shape your path.

Build your future in tech—develop cybersecurity tools, network simulators, or 3D games. Learn to design and implement software from the ground up through a dynamic, project-based curriculum. Graduate with real-world experience and in-demand skills.

Combine classroom learning, lab work, and field experiences to explore the Geosciences. Work with industry-standard equipment and engage in faculty-guided research while building problem-solving skills to tackle global issues like water resources, environmental analysis, natural hazards, and sustainable energy.

Jump into the study of human movement, health and wellness as you learn about physical activity, exercise and rehabilitation. With biomechanics, exercise science and molecular exercise physiology laboratories, you can learn by doing while serving the community. Through our options in Exercise Science, Public Health and Sport and Social Justice, you can tailor your education to your dream career.

Put your passion for fitness and sports into action while providing youth with healthy exercise habits and teamwork skills they will carry with them for the rest of their lives. Encourage healthy living and make a meaningful and lasting difference. Prepare for teaching credential programs and careers in physical education from elementary to high school.

Extend your knowledge and impact as you study mathematical, statistical, computational and modeling methods to solve real-world issues across industries like engineering, finance, health and technology. With the applied mathematics / statistics program emphasis, you will find extensive opportunities to make a difference in others’ lives.

Add value to students’ lives and make math accessible as you prepare for a career in teaching or explore the depths of pure mathematics. This program emphasizes secondary teacher preparation or pure math, equipping you with skills to teach or advance mathematical knowledge.

Contribute to transformational medical and technological advancements at the intersection of physics and biology. The Biophysics option provides multidisciplinary preparation to apply physical principles to biological and medical problems, including basic and applied research, careers in biomedical and biotechnology industries, professional studies for clinical careers, and science education.

Explore topics from classical mechanics to interstellar processes with the General Physics option. Choose an emphasis in Astrophysics or General to match your interests and goals. Theory courses are paired with labs and hands-on activities, giving you practical experience and a strong foundation in physics and its applications.

Share your passion for physics or explore other natural sciences with the Integrated Science option. Gain strong physics and quantitative skills, a broad science education, and communication tools for careers in education or education policy, all while understanding the history and nature of science.

Become an impactful educator in the lives of young children as you help them develop foundational skills, foster positive relationships, and discover a love of learning that will support them for the rest of their lives. Through your influence, children can learn to be resilient, welcome and persist in problem-solving, resolve conflict, and develop an early appreciation for inquiry-based learning.

major: Early Childhood Studies Integrated Teacher Education Program Education Specialist: Extensive Support Needs
description: Become an advocate for all children by fostering inclusive environments and providing the tools they need to thrive. In just four years, earn a B.A. in Early Childhood Studies and a Special Education credential. This option is for those interested in working with children in extensive support classrooms.

major: Early Childhood Studies Integrated Teacher Education Program Education Specialist: Mild to Moderate Support Needs
description: Create inclusive spaces where every child feels valued and empowered. Earn a B.A. in Early Childhood Studies and a Special Education credential in four years. This option is for those who want to work with children in mild to moderate support classrooms.

Translate your passion for language and serving diverse students into a career in multilingual education for young children. The Multilingual Teaching option is one of the few programs in higher education that provides this unique training. You will be prepared to enter a growing field and connect students with language and culture through immersive instruction.

Make a transformational impact on young children and families in diverse contexts beyond the classroom. Prepare for careers in social work, child life, school psychology, counseling and therapy, foster care, advocacy and more. The Non-Teaching pathway gives you the flexibility to choose courses within our department to tailor your education to your desired career path.

Help young learners build foundational skills in problem solving, relationships, and inquiry. The Pre-K to Grade 3 option equips ADT transfer students with the preparation needed to become TK teachers through coursework in teacher prep and child development.

Are you trying to decide between your many interests? Here, you won’t have to. Pursue interdisciplinary knowledge as you explore various subjects, from arts and humanities to math and natural sciences. With the General Studies pathway, you will create your own degree to reach your dream profession, whether graduate school or a career in the nonprofit, corporate, public health or education sectors.

major: Liberal Studies Integrated Teacher Education Program Education Specialist: Extensive Support Needs
description: Foster inclusive learning environments where every child can succeed. Through a mix of liberal studies and special education, you will learn how to support children with diverse needs. In the ITEP Extensive Support option, you will take ten core liberal studies courses, then add to your base knowledge with classes in special education and clinical practice in an extensive support classroom.

major: Liberal Studies Integrated Teacher Education Program Education Specialist: Mild to Moderate Support Needs
description: Provide the tools and support that all children need to thrive. Combine liberal studies and special education as you gain the skills to teach children with diverse learning needs. In the ITEP Mild/Moderate Support option, you will take ten core liberal studies courses, then add to your base knowledge with classes in special education and clinical practice in a mild to moderate support classroom.

Pursue your passion for teaching and shaping young minds with an interdisciplinary liberal arts education. Help children develop foundational skills and a love of learning that will support them for the rest of their lives. Build the skills, knowledge and disposition to work with children from kindergarten to grade 8 and graduate ready to take on a credential program.

Build a deep understanding of human diversity and use it to make a real-world impact. The applied anthropology option blends theory with hands-on training in research and cultural analysis, preparing you to tackle social issues, analyze human behavior, translate insights into solutions and communicate effectively across diverse communities.

Discover the ancient world through archaeology, the study of human history and cultures through material remains. This option provides a strong understanding of the techniques used to uncover and interpret the physical evidence of past cultures and the research and critical thinking skills needed to shape the future. It prepares you for both professional and academic opportunities in archaeology.

Gain a deeper understanding of humanity, culture and change over time. The general anthropology degree offers a broad, four-field approach to the discipline, providing a strong foundation for graduate study or careers in education, law, social services, government or international work.

Study the relationships between people, places and the natural environment. Be at the forefront of crucial topics like climate change, natural resource management and human geography – the exploration of how people impact and interact with their environment. You will combine scientific analysis with practical skills, preparing to address environmental issues and promote sustainable practices.

Manage and interpret geographic data to help institutions better understand our environment through the Geospatial Analysis option. You will learn and develop technical skills, including Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and Remote Sensing software. Graduate prepared for a future dedicated to land-use management, local government and environmental protection.

Solve complex organizational challenges with skills in communication across personal, organizational, and cultural settings. This research-based program blends theory and practice, preparing you for careers in training, consulting, and organizational development.

Craft compelling stories that shape communities and inspire change. Multimedia journalism prepares you for roles in news, nonprofit, magazine, and digital media. Build a digital portfolio while mastering writing, video, and multimedia skills for diverse platforms and audiences.

Drive strategic communication between organizations and stakeholders. Gain hands-on experience in campaign creation, crisis management, and digital engagement. Build expertise in messaging, media relations, and analytics through coursework, internships, and client projects.

Explore the foundations of human behavior through developmental, social, cognitive, clinical, and physiological psychology. Gain critical skills in research methods and statistics, with opportunities for original research. Whether aiming for graduate school or a career in management, public service, or beyond, this program offers a strong foundation.

Gain in-demand skills in economic analysis and become a valuable asset to business or government. The Applied Economics option emphasizes hands-on learning and real-world applications such as banking, regulation, and economic forecasting.

Build a solid foundation in economics while tailoring your coursework to your interests. The General Economics option combines applied and theoretical approaches to prepare you for careers in business, public policy, law, and more.

Apply your math skills to economic theory with the Quantitative Economics option. Designed for students with strong math backgrounds, this program prepares you for careers in finance, risk analysis, and advanced study in technical fields.

Explore how language works and apply it to real-world challenges. In Applied Language Studies, gain skills for careers in education, communication, policy, media, business, and more. Complete a capstone project on a linguistics topic of your choice.

Inspire the next generation through literature, writing, and language. English Education prepares you to become a middle or high school English teacher with both theory and hands-on classroom experience, leading to a single-subject credential.

Dive into global literature and cultural texts in the Literary Studies program. Explore diverse eras and genres while building skills in writing, analysis, and critical thinking. Prepare for careers in writing, media, publishing, or graduate study.

Gain advanced Spanish proficiency and explore the cultural diversity of the Spanish-speaking world. Study the language’s structure, its role in bilingualism, and its impact on communication, education, and literacy. Courses in writing, translation, literature, and media build skills in analysis, cultural competency, and meaningful global connection.

Explore how identities, cultures, and histories shape our world through the GEMS program. Choose from areas like African American, Asian Pacific Islander, Chicana/o Latina/o, Native American, or Gender and Sexuality Studies. The Pre-Credential Option blends GEMS with education courses for a teaching career.

major: Gender, Ethnicity, and Multicultural Studies - Pre-Credential
description: Inspire young minds and champion inclusion with the GEMS Pre-Credential Option. This unique path combines cultural studies and teaching preparation, equipping you to build classrooms where every student feels seen, valued, and empowered.

Understand the complex relationship between the past and contemporary social, political and cultural issues. Develop your research and analysis skills, build historical arguments, and become a better-informed global citizen. With the General History option, you'll have the freedom to explore your interests or complement your degree with a minor.

Help future generations understand the world by sharing our past. Explore diverse regions and eras through a comprehensive history curriculum and gain the skills to teach social sciences. This program prepares you to pursue a teaching credential with confidence and impact.

Dive into music with the General Music option, where performance, technology, and industry knowledge come together. Guided by expert faculty, explore theory, history, and trends while building a solid foundation and the freedom to pursue interdisciplinary interests.

Turn your passion for music into a career with the Music Industry Studies option. Learn production, marketing, management, and the business of music. Gain hands-on experience through internships and collaborations in the vibrant Los Angeles music scene.

Transform your musical ideas into original works with the Music Composition option. Study techniques, orchestration, and contemporary practices while creating music with advanced tech. Collaborate with peers and gain experience through performances of your own compositions.

Inspire the next generation of musicians through our Pedagogy (Pre-Credential) program. Learn the theory and practice of teaching music in schools while gaining hands-on experience. This program prepares you for a Single Subject Credential in Music.

Elevate your music skills and performance artistry with the Music Performance option. Specialize in your instrument or voice while performing solo and in ensembles. Hone your technique and grow your unique musical voice through extensive hands-on experience.

Ready to sharpen your mind and tackle tough questions? The General Philosophy option challenges you to think critically, break down complex ideas, and connect concepts across fields. Explore the big picture by combining logic, ethics, and reasoning to form well-rounded perspectives for science, technology, media, and more.

Interested in making a tangible impact on society? The Law and Society option blends deep philosophical thinking with hands-on problem-solving, focusing on the ethical, social and political issues that shape our world. You’ll dive into the complexities of law and justice, learning to analyze legal concepts and tackle societal challenges with both reason and compassion.

Address problems raised by AI’s increasingly pervasive influence on society—problems such as algorithmic bias and the question of how to address it; moral and legal responsibility for AI decision making; displacement of a wide range of human jobs from computer coding to truck driving; and the environmental impacts of AI. Effectively addressing these problems requires skill in negotiating competing values and acute sensitivity to the social and cultural contexts in which AI’s harms and benefits arise.

Tackle big questions at the intersection of science, technology, and society. The STS program combines natural sciences, tech, humanities, and social sciences to explore how these fields influence and reflect the world. Study the impacts of breakthroughs and innovations while solving real-world problems through history, ethics, and critical thinking.

Become a changemaker with a deep understanding of American government, global diplomacy, public law, and political theory. Learn how policies are made, how governments function, and how you can make an impact. Small classes and hands-on learning build the skills needed for careers in politics, diplomacy, law, social justice, and more.

Lead in the construction industry by blending civil engineering and business. Learn structural engineering, project management, and cost estimation. Hands-on labs and practical coursework prepare you for careers in commercial, heavy-civil, or residential construction.

Gain a solid foundation in classic and contemporary sociological theories and investigate the structure of groups, organizations, and societies and how people interact within these contexts. The General Sociology option lays the groundwork for you to pursue grad school in a variety of focuses like law or public administration or jump into careers in social services, public policy, or business.

Do you dream of making a real impact on people’s lives and strengthening communities? Our Social Work Option combines the power of sociology with practical tools to help you do just that. You’ll dive into important real-world issues like mental health, child welfare and elder care and gain valuable hands-on experience to prepare you for graduate school or a rewarding career in social services.

Bring characters to life, explore the depths of human emotion and explore the craft of storytelling through your body, voice and presence. Graduate with the skills to captivate an audience, evoke empathy and transform any script into a living, breathing experience.

Use movement and musicality to express emotion and reflect on life, culture, and society. Study dance history and develop a global perspective of the art. Train in various styles and gain theatre skills for a well-rounded education that prepares you for a career as a performer or professional in the entertainment industry.

Feel the energy of the stage at your fingertips as you experiment with technological advancements in design and technical production. Build a comprehensive foundation of production principles, then examine and apply modern approaches. With our emphasis on the “doing” of theatre, you will develop a robust portfolio you can be proud of.

Explore all a theatre degree has to offer through the General Theatre option. Experience a broad curriculum and focus on areas like directing, playwriting, management, or theory and criticism. Customize your education to match your career goals and build the skills to thrive in the performing arts industry.

major: Theatre in Education and Community Engagement
description: Use performance as a tool for social change, personal growth, and community building. Learn to craft stories that engage, inspire, and challenge. Gain skills to lead workshops, create educational theatre, and drive community projects that connect people, spark dialogue, and empower others through the transformative power of theatre.

college: The Collins College of Hospitality Management
description: In our hospitality management program, you’ll learn what it takes to run everything from restaurants to resorts to global events and entertainment companies. With hands-on experiences and mentoring by industry leaders, you’ll develop analytical, marketing, human resources, teamwork and service excellence — and graduate career-ready, confident and ready to lead life’s most exciting moments.
